title.value: Tohle není Open Source repo, to je jen dump kódu na GitHubu: Co s tím?

summary.value: The Czech version of my reusable repositories talk at the Frontendisti Brno March meetup: why a GitHub repository is a product interface for other developers, and which non-functional pieces (README, automation, documentation, meta files) turn a code dump into an open source project.

value.description: Tohle není Open Source repo, to je jen dump kódu na GitHubu: Co s tím?

content.value:
What the session covered

"This is not an open source repo, it's just a code dump on GitHub: what now?" The talk is about everything around the code: the non-functional requirements and meta features that decide whether anyone can reuse your repository. It draws on my experience building SDKs, dev tools, starters, and integration packages.

  • A repository is a product interface: other developers meet your README before they meet your code.
  • README structure: installation, a getting started example, code samples, links to docs, contact, and license.
  • Automation and community files: templates, contributing guides, and checks that keep a project healthy without manual effort.
  • Documentation and best practices: what to write down so contributors and users do not have to ask.

The venue

The Frontendisti Brno March meetup, Wednesday March 11, 2026 at AIS Servis in Brno, with 56 attendees. I shared the evening with Vilém Lipold, Martin Brychta (Superkoders), and Lukáš Chylík (AIS Servis). The talk is in Czech; the English version ran at Python Pizza Ostrava a few weeks earlier.
